cycles.title: Cycle Views
cycles.description: Audience-specific views over the APIOps Cycles method
cycle.capability-productization-cycle.de: A cycle for defining and productizing reusable digital capabilities without assuming the implementation style in advance.
cycle.capability-productization-cycle.pu: Guide reusable capability definition from hypothesis and consumer/producer requirements through architecture, solution design, delivery, readiness, publishing, and continuous improvement.
cycle.api-productization-cycle.title: API Productization Cycle
cycle.api-productization-cycle.descripti: The API-focused APIOps Cycles journey for productizing, designing, delivering, publishing, and improving APIs.
cycle.api-productization-cycle.purpose: API-focused method journey for teams that already know the intended implementation style is an API product.
cycle.integration-productization-cycle.d: A cycle for defining and productizing reusable integration capabilities without assuming the implementation style in advance.
cycle.integration-productization-cycle.p: Guide reusable integration capability design before choosing an API, event, file, stream, data product, direct integration, or hybrid implementation style.
cycle.api-productization-cycle.station.a: Frame the API as a product with clear value proposition, consumers, business model, ownership, and lifecycle intent.
Define API consumer segments, onboarding paths, expectations, and experience requirements before design decisions are locked.
Choose and validate the API platform, architecture, governance, and operational constraints needed for the product.
Design the API contract, interaction model, schemas, policies, and usability details before implementation.
Implement, test, secure, automate, and operate the API product through the delivery pipeline.
Validate API quality, compliance, evidence, operational readiness, and release criteria.
Publish the API product so consumers can discover it, evaluate it, request access, complete onboarding, use it, and get support.
cycle.api-productization-cycle.station.m: Monitor API health, adoption, consumer outcomes, reliability, and improvement opportunities after release.
cycle.automation-cycle.title: Automation Cycle
cycle.automation-cycle.description: A cycle for selecting, designing, delivering, enabling, and improving automation solutions across people, rules, workflows, agents, integrations, UI automation, and operations.
cycle.automation-cycle.purpose: Guide teams from external customer and capability outcomes to a validated, governed, and operable automation solution.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-produ: Start from the most external meaningful customer. Reuse journey and capability-value evidence to validate whether an automation hypothesis should proceed.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-consu: Clarify the process, experience, domain, service, and non-functional requirements that the later workflow and architecture must satisfy.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-platf: Use impact, location, capacity, and earlier requirements to choose the automation implementation approach and record the rationale and remaining risks.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-desig: Design the internal workflow needed to deliver the selected customer and capability outcomes, including work allocation, controls, exceptions, recovery, evidence, and monitoring.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-deliv: Build, configure, test, version, deploy, and prepare the operating model for the selected automation path, including ownership, environments, runbooks, monitoring, fallback, rollback, support, and known risks.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-audit: Use a readiness checklist to review evidence and record the release decision: ready, ready with conditions, remediation required, or not approved.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-publi: Activate and roll out the automation safely with communications, training, operating instructions, support paths, adoption monitoring, feedback channels, phased rollout, pause, and rollback conditions.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.monitorin: Monitor actual automation outcomes, run success and failure, exceptions, retries, interventions, cycle time, waiting time, cost, errors, unsafe actions, adoption, trust, realized benefit, and which hypothesis assumptions were supported or rejected.
cycle.integration-productization-cycle.s: Start from customer journey, capability value, and viability evidence, then validate whether the proposed reusable integration capability should proceed.
Agree provider and consumer commitments for access, validation, service, failure handling, recovery, compatibility, and lifecycle.
Select the integration architecture, implementation style, and platform capabilities, taking account of constraints and the governance model.
Design the integration solution, contracts, schemas, data structures, mappings, and interaction or delivery patterns for the selected style.
Build, test, deploy, and operate the integration capability using its selected implementation style and validated contract.
Assure integration readiness, governance, quality, security, compliance, and operational evidence before release.
Publish the integration capability so teams can discover it, evaluate it, request access, complete onboarding, reuse it, and get support.
Monitor integration reliability, reuse, incidents, performance, consumer outcomes, and improvement needs.
cycle.capability-productization-cycle.st: Start from customer journey, capability value, and viability evidence, then validate whether the proposed reusable digital capability should proceed.
Agree mutual owner, producer, and consumer commitments for access, service, support, change, and lifecycle.
Select the capability implementation style, architecture pattern, enabling platform, and governance model from evidence.
Design how consumers access, interact with, receive, or use the capability through the selected implementation style.
Deliver and operate the reusable capability using implementation-style-appropriate engineering, testing, security, release, support, and operational ownership practices.

Review capability readiness using evidence from solution design, contract or service definition, testing, operations, permissions, monitoring, support, fallback, lifecycle, risk, and ownership before release.
Publish the reusable capability so intended consumers can discover it, understand its purpose and service expectations, request access, onboard, use it, and get support.
Monitor capability value, outcomes, adoption, reuse, service health, consumer experience, cost, sustainability, and lifecycle improvement needs.
